It is not only the bad players that ruin the fun it's the Dev's/Stewards and rules for contact.
 
A crash caused by someone losing control and taking you out unintentionally can take you from a trusted driver with a green badge to a red warning bad driver badge in one crash, 
e.g. massive multy car crash on Le Mans straight will do it. 
You get punished because someone else can’t drive or race. You get a message to say you crash to much, you are a bad driver and must improve even if you are not at fault.

The daily racers are brutal, on average 20% to 33% of the grid will crash out within the 1st 3 corners/bends on the 1st lap, another 10% will crash out due to people fighting for position for the remainder of the race.
The 1st few drivers and maybe some in the top 10 may enjoy the race at times but the tail end is usually frustrated, abusive and demoralised by both players and the safety rating system

You are not allowed to protest any of the above situations, those rules are not enforced by the Devs/stewards.

You get 3 protests a month.
If you are right and the situation was intentional wrecking then you get a protest back.
If you make a protest and the dev/Stewards call it driver error or they think it was not intentional wrecking you get punished by having your protests reduced for the month.
When your 3 protests are gone you have no way of protesting other bad players, so a lot of bad players won’t get punished for ruining yours and others race.

I really wanted to like this sim, honestly, but it's really impossible at the current state of things.
I strongly recommend holding off from buying this until it is actually stable enough to race in, there are so many issues with it it's baffling.

[b]1) Force feedback doesn't work on Moza wheelbases[/b]
Out of the box, the feedback you get is atrocious. The balance of the FFB components is all over the place, I've spent ~100 hours of playtime over a month just getting it to somewhat acceptable feeling using 3rd party apps (LMUFFB) since I couldn't get any FFB that felt acceptable with in-game and Moza pithouse settings.
The wheel would violently oscillate on straights, ABS and brake lockups vibrate so much it's impossible to control while turning into corners, there's zero feedback when your rear end steps out, and the list goes on.

[b]2) Patches[/b]
Continuing on (1), from the info I've gathered debugging the unusable FFB, others have said this problem was introduced with 1.4 update. It has now been a month since that update, yet the issue is still not fixed. For something as game-breaking as this for a decent percentage of people, this is deeply concerning, firstly that the update was not tested, then that it wasn't fixed for this long. Being out for a whole month and still counting is just unacceptable.
This does not give me the confidence that I want in order to transition to LMU as my primary sim, or even drive in it since I could spend that time racing in another one. 

[b]3) Paid servers[/b]
I am not against this as a whole, it makes it easier and more accessible for many people to have their own servers and not deal with the technical side of setting it up and maintaining it, and the prices are reasonable.
However, forcing people into this as an only option is awful and feels like an additional cash grab. You have to pay for the base game, DLCs, race control subscription, and still have to pay hourly for a private server? I've hosted practice servers for my endurance teammates in ACC with no problems, but here it's not possible?

[b]4) AI[/b]
I get that this is not a priority at the moment, but if you use AI as a practice tool as I do, prepare for endless frustration. Even at the lowest AI aggression setting, it will still rear-end you, squeeze you off track, change lines right in front of you out of nowhere, brake 50 meters before the braking point with no one in front of it, and this list also goes on.
Even in the same class this is problematic, but with multiclass it is a hundred times worse.
With talks of a single-player campaign mode coming soon, I really don't see it being any good if the AI doesn't get a huge overhaul in the meantime.

[b]5) Controls[/b]
A bit of a nitpick, but the control binding situation is horrid. Not being able to map TC/ABS potentiometers properly and no support for shift keys for additional layers really makes the keyboard and/or some other kind of controller mandatory alongside the wheel.
I get that having to support all the different input devices on the market is not easy, but at least give us the ability to make plugins with access to car controls, there is already fields in the shared memory with most of them, they just aren't writable.

[b]6) Optimizations[/b]
Definitely not the prettiest game out there, which is really fine, all the eye-candy is a cherry on top for all sims, but making it run this poorly really is disappointing.

After 6 years and ~1000 hours of AC/ACC, I’ve finally tried out LMU.  It’s been terrible and wonderful.  For context of my review, I am not a RaceControl Pro subscriber; I only purchase the DLC and do the daily races.

Let’s start with the good:
•	The online match making is great. It puts drivers together with similar skill that other sims just don’t have.
•	Graphics are great.
•	It really is the most realistic sim I’ve tried.

On to the bad:
My main issue is that so much of the software is unfinished or poorly designed.  It makes everything feel unfinished. 
•	Force feedback is a disaster.
o	Some cars are completely UNDRIVEABLE for me due to oscillations/vibrations while simply driving straight.  If I’m driving straight and let go of my wheel, it will immediately start oscillating and crash the car into a wall.  I CANNOT UNDERSTAND HOW THIS IS ACCEPTABLE AND PASSES QC EVERY PATCH.  My hardware is only 2 years old and my software is always up to date.
o	My wheel feels like it’s being ground to dust the entire time I’m driving.  I have serious concerns if this is creating any long term damage  
•	The Safety Rating system doesn’t make sense to me.
o	“High” SR penalties for colliding with a wall after car contact just adds insult to injury.  If it’s my fault, it’s already bad; it doesn’t need to be worse.  If it’s the other driver’s fault, it’s infuriating.  
o	Track limits infractions for avoiding cars that are crashing or parked on the track.  This is completely unacceptable.  
o	I do not understand why there are Safety Rating changes, good or bad, for activities during qualifying, when there are no other cars on track.
o	Using a Joker literally doesn’t do anything to my ratings.  I don’t see anything change at all.
o	“High” SR penalties for getting rammed from behind because somebody missed their braking point is terrible.
•	The user interface is terrible, poorly designed, and buggy. 
o	Slow/unresponsive.  When I finish an offline race, there’s literally no where to click to go back to the main menu, so I have to alt + F4 it.  This is completely unacceptable.
o	You cannot properly map dial switches on your wheel to various ABS/TC/Map settings like you can in literally every other sim.  I do not understand how a sim based on realism has missed this.
•	The racing experience is constantly frustrating.
o	Constant track limit evaluations, with most resulting in no action, are very distracting.
o	The start procedure graphics/interface is one of the worst user experiences I’ve ever had.  It’s confusing and there are no instructions.  I had to resort to watching videos on YouTube, and even then, I still get confusing penalties. I’ve finally learned to 100% ignore it, and now I’m fine. 
•	Missing tire slip telemetry data.
•	No useful data after the session/race has ended.  Want to see you lap times? Nope.

To conclude, I’m very frustrated every time I boot this software up.  I think most of my concerns are easily fixable, and I expect most to improve with time.  LMU will likely become the only place I do GT3 racing, but I cannot give this a top rating if they make me keep paying money and while having all kinds of quality control issues.

You have to understand the limits of the car.

ACC would be at the same level if it had daily races or organized events, and that’s the big advantage of Le Mans Ultimate.

Better than Gran Turismo, it offers realism with real-time damage.
You can throw an endurance race of 4 hours in 7 minutes because the engine blew up… I know what I’m talking about.

I still don’t know how it compares to iRacing, but LMU gives you many circuits with the base game, without any subscription.
At Bronze level, you don’t need any DLC except for cars if you want them.
Daily races with DLC content only start at Silver and above.

The subscription isn’t required. It gives you access to some events, but you need to be at least Silver.
It also gives small bonuses, but nothing major.

I recommend this game as the best starter into sim racing.

LMU has the potential to be a great racing sim, but the online experience completely ruins it.

The connectivity is terrible. Disconnects, server issues, and general instability make it hard to enjoy multiplayer consistently. Nothing is more frustrating than putting time into practice and qualifying just for the game or server to screw you over.

The penalty and ban system is even worse. It feels inconsistent and does a terrible job of distinguishing between someone intentionally driving like an idiot and someone getting caught up in an incident. You can get punished heavily for something you had little or no control over, while people who constantly cause wrecks somehow keep showing up in races.

And the actual racing? Half the time it feels like bumper cars with a damage model. People divebomb from ridiculous distances, shove their way through corners, and use other cars as brakes. The only difference between LMU and an arcade demolition derby is that LMU will actually destroy your car afterward and ruin the rest of your race.

That is probably the most frustrating part. LMU tries to be a serious endurance racing simulator, but the multiplayer environment often doesn't encourage serious racing. When contact has major consequences, the stewarding, matchmaking, connectivity, and penalty systems need to be good enough to support that. Right now, they aren't.

The driving itself can be fun, but the online experience makes it incredibly difficult to recommend. If I wanted bumper cars, I'd play something that doesn't require me to spend 20 minutes practicing first.

Writing this review as follow-up to the release of version 1.4:

This Racing Simulator had it's major strength in it's build in Multiplayer. Which had its flaws, but was just easy to use, had a nice netcode with exceptional collision physics and mostly fair matchmaking.

BUT after the release of V1.4, Things changed. Making the online experience awful and sometimes unplayable. The change in network protocol and other backend systems cause servers to crash mid game, people are now teleporting instead of disappearing which suddenly leaves one getting sideswiped for non reason and having the race ended for one.
EVEN if you manage to dodge all the malfunctions, you better hope to be racing a sprint race. Because of changes in the pitstops, Cars now can get stuck in pits because they are to close to eachother. When the Car is being rotated, Cars happen to clip throug the ground beacuse they get pushed thru it from another car that pits, or the other car simply damages your freshly services car. nice. As icing on the cake, in Single-Player those issues cause the NPC Drivers to also crash in pits, get damage and block the fast lane.

According to multiple sources, those issues were mention on release day of 1.4V! 2 Weeks later, it's still a mess!

The Game is not in Early Accses anymore, but still gets treated like one by the devs.

The promised Carrer-Mode is still absent and not announced, but atleast there are new tracks which are ok, but on the expensive side and also full of issues.

The Game often feels bland and heartless in different apparments, like sound design, UI, and Ranking system.

Some Online Races are often simply unfair, because of very poor balancing. f.e. Racing 45min Interlagos with LMGT3s, puts one to an extra pitstip if you dont drive the Lexus. (could be also fixed with a mandatory pitstop function)

Practicing is a chore, since it takes alot of clicks to setup the track in best conditions.

I'd simply stay away from this money pit for some time, until real fixes happen without bringing more problems with them. (4 out of 4 Streak since V1.0) Don't play it, no matter if you like single player racing or online multiplayer.

The basics of the game is great. 
The safety rating system and driver ranking system is AWFUL. For context, I have over 1.5k hours on iRacing, a consistent B-License Sports Car License and occasionally get into A class. I'm by no means a pro or in the top 10%, but LMU's system hurts the average player. 

LMU's safety rating/driver ranking system is comprised of 3 pieces; 
- Driver Ranking
- Safety Rating
- Recent Performance Rating

Your recent performance rating takes your most recent races and evaluates their safety, and determines who you get grouped with. Not based on driver skill or overall average safety rating, just your most recent few races. 
Let's say you have a bad race and crash, DNF. Happens. Next race, if you do not have an EXTREMELY CLEAN RACE with NO contact, you will move down on the recent performance rating. There are a green/blue thumbs up, a neutral, and an orange/red exclamation point. Once you are in the "!" category, you are ONLY racing with people who crash. It creates a domino effect where you can NEVER recover you safety rating, unless you either get 1) Lucky with your split and have decent racing, or 2) You just can't race, and have to drive solely to avoid contact. 
Because the game cannot determine fault of incident, nearly ANY contact penalizes you. 
I finished 3rd in a GT3 race at LeMans. I was REAR ENDED SO HARD IT PUSHED ME OFF THE TRACK 200ft, AND I GOT A 24HR SUSPENSION. 

When you have a system like this, mixed in CONTROLLER PLAYERS (...), there is almost zero incentive to play any LMU events compared to iRacing events. Netcode and graphics, that's it. 

To top it off, if you get stuck in this loop, it means you are stuck to whatever the daily bronze races are.

LMU: Lousy, Mediocre, Underdeveloped

I regret all the money I spent on this scam. This is an rFactor 2 mod disquised as a game and priced an insane amount of money for what it's worth. A mod for a 15 year old, bugged game at that. It has no redeeming features: all cars handle terribly. It's just insane amounts of understeer. Unless you want to exit a slow corner, then there's snap-oversteer. The LMGT3 cars in this joke of a game, are supposed to reflect real LMGT3 cars: vehicles made with gentleman drivers in mind. Yet they handle so horribly it's beyond belief any of those gentleman drivers would pay any money to race them if they behaved like that in real life. Traction control simulation is an absolute joke. ABS simulation is good, that's basically the only thing they got right phisics wise. Flat spot simulation is overdone. I drove cars on slicks in real life, had my fair share of lockups and spins and at no point did I get such insane flatspots as from a small lockup in LMU. The list goes on.
There are no safety cars, puddles in the rain are merely a visual aspect (ACC could simulate them many years ago but apparently this rfactor2 paid mod can't), windshield wipers on the mclaren are bugged and don't remove water from your windshield etc.
Online play? Another joke: if someone rams you in the first corner wrecking your car you can't even DNF because if you do, the stupid excuse for a simulator will punish your safety rating because you didn't finish. Like what is the actual point of this in a 20 minute daily sprint!? What real life mechanism is simulated here!? None, racing in real life is actually easier than in this joke of a simulator. I tried both, I suggest you save any money you would spend for this game and go to a local gokart track or something like that. It will be a lot more enjoyable and a lot less frustrating.

Oh yes, money: DLC's cost a ridiculous amount of it. Plus they are now implementing a mechanism that will allow you to write off one bad race. Sounds like a good idea to solve that DNF problem I mentioned above? Well it would be if it wasn't for the fact that it will only be available for those that pay a monthly subscription. Yes, it's this shameless. It designs a terrible system specifically to make you pay for ways to bypass it's worst parts. This alone warrants a negative review.

EDIT Forgot to write about the UI: it's absolutely horrible, the worst in any recent game. Every click makes you wait for a LMU logo animation to appear and disappear. It's also bugged: sometimes it blocks the "Join Practice" button for no reason in online races and you have to close and reopen the game for it to start working. And you have to do it several times. And even if it does appear, sometimes the servers are greyed out and you can't join unless you restart again. And you can see the servers are running because it shows player numbers. Bugged and hopeless. So that's another reason not to buy it
